en: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah; (H) and Abu Kurayb and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim both narrated to us from Waki', Sufyan narrated to us—both of them from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir, from the Prophet (pbuh), with the meaning of the hadith of Ibn 'Uyaynah.

Amr al-Naqid narrated to us, Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, who said: I heard him saying: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) called upon the people to volunteer on the day of the Trench, and al-Zubayr volunteered. Then he called upon them again, and al-Zubayr volunteered. Then he called upon them again, and al-Zubayr volunteered. Thereupon the Prophet (pbuh) said: "Every prophet has a disciple, and my disciple is al-Zubayr."

Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami, Hamid ibn 'Umar al-Bakrawi, and Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us—they said: al-Mu'tamir—and he is Ibn Sulayman—narrated to us, he said: I heard my father narrating from Abu 'Uthman, who said: None remained with the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) on one of those days in which the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) fought, other than Talhah and Sa'd—from their narration.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah al-Asadi narrated to us, from Isra'il, from al-Miqdam ibn Shurayh, from his father, from Sa'd, who said: We were six individuals with the Prophet (pbuh), and the idolaters said to the Prophet (pbuh): "Drive these ones away so that they do not become insolent toward us." He said: And they were myself, Ibn Mas'ud, a man from Hudhayl, Bilal, and two men whom I will not name. There occurred in the heart of the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) whatever Allah willed to occur, and he spoke to himself; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "And do not send away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance."

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Miqdam ibn Shurayh, from his father, from Sa'd: Concerning me was revealed: "And do not send away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening." He said: It was revealed concerning six, among whom were myself and Ibn Mas'ud; and the idolaters had said to him: "Do you bring these close?"

Muhammad ibn 'Abbad narrated to us, Hatim—meaning Ibn Isma'il—narrated to us, from Bukayr ibn Mismar, from 'Amir ibn Sa'd, from his father, that the Prophet (pbuh) combined both his parents for him on the day of Uhud. He said: There was a man among the idolaters who had burned the Muslims, so the Prophet (pbuh) said to him: "Shoot, may my father and mother be ransomed for you!" He said: So I drew an arrow without an arrowhead for him and struck his side, so that he fell down and his private area was exposed, and the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) laughed until I could see his molar teeth.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id and Ibn Rumh narrated to us from al-Layth ibn Sa'd; (H) and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us—both of them from Yahya ibn Sa'id, with this chain of narration.

Abdullah ibn Maslamah ibn Qa'nab narrated to us, Sulayman—meaning Ibn Bilal—narrated to us, from Yahya—and he is Ibn Sa'id—from Sa'id, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) combined both his parents for me on the day of Uhud.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar both narrated to us—they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us; (H) and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us; (H) and Abu Kurayb and Ishaq al-Hanzali narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Bishr, from Mis'ar; (H) and Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Mis'ar—all of them from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, from 'Abdullah ibn Shaddad, from 'Ali, from the Prophet (pbuh), the like of it.

Mansur ibn Abi Muzahim narrated to us, Ibrahim—meaning Ibn Sa'd—narrated to us, from his father, from 'Abdullah ibn Shaddad, who said: I heard 'Ali saying: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) never combined both his parents for anyone except Sa'd ibn Malik; for on the day of Uhud he kept saying to him: "Shoot, may my father and mother be ransomed for you!"

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated it to us, 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, I heard Yahya ibn Sa'id saying: I heard 'Abdullah ibn 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah saying: 'A'ishah said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) was unable to sleep one night... with the like of the hadith of Sulayman ibn Bilal.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Layth narrated to us; (H) and Muhammad ibn Rumh narrated to us, al-Layth informed us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah, that 'A'ishah said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) stayed awake one night upon his arrival in Medina and said: "Would that a righteous man from my Companions would guard me tonight." She said: While we were like that, we heard the clatter of weapons. He said: "Who is this?" He said: "Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas." The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: "What brought you?" He said: "Fear for the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) occurred in my heart, so I came to guard him." So the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) supplicated for him and then slept. And in the narration of Ibn Rumh: "So we said: Who is this?"

Abdullah ibn Maslamah ibn Qa'nab narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Bilal narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah, from 'A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) was unable to sleep one night, so he said: "Would that a righteous man from my Companions would guard me tonight." She said: And we heard the sound of weapons, so the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: "Who is this?" He said: "Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, O Messenger of Allah; I have come to guard you." 'A'ishah said: So the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) slept until I heard his snoring.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz—meaning Ibn Abi Hazim—narrated to us, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, who said: A man from the family of Marwan was appointed governor over Medina. He said: He summoned Sahl ibn Sa'd and ordered him to revile 'Ali. He said: Sahl refused. So he said to him: "Since you refuse, then say: 'May Allah curse Abu al-Turab.'" Sahl said: "There was no name more beloved to 'Ali than Abu al-Turab, and he used to be delighted whenever he was called by it." He said to him: "Tell us about his story; why was he named Abu Turab?" Sahl said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) came to the house of Fatimah, but did not find 'Ali in the house. He said: "Where is your cousin?" She said: "There was something between him and me, so he became upset with me and left, and did not take his midday nap with me." The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said to a person: "Go and see where he is." He returned and said: "O Messenger of Allah, he is sleeping in the mosque." So the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) came to him while he was lying down, his cloak having fallen off his side, and dust had gotten upon him. The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) began wiping it off him and saying: "Get up, O Abu al-Turab! Get up, O Abu al-Turab!"

Muhammad ibn Bakkar ibn al-Rayyan narrated to us, Hassan—meaning Ibn Ibrahim—narrated to us, from Sa'id—and he is Ibn Masruq—from Yazid ibn Hayyan, from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: We entered upon him and said to him: "You have indeed witnessed much good. You accompanied the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) and prayed behind him..." and he related the hadith similar to the hadith of Abu Hayyan, except that he said: "Behold, I am leaving among you two weighty things: one of them is the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; it is the rope of Allah—whoever follows it is upon guidance, and whoever abandons it is upon misguidance." And in it: We said: "Who are the people of his household? Are his wives among them?" He said: "No, by Allah; a woman stays with a man for a period of time, then he divorces her and she returns to her father and her people. The people of his household are his origin and his agnatic relatives who were forbidden from accepting charity after him."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us; (H) and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Jarir informed us—both of them from Abu Hayyan, with this chain of narration, similar to the hadith of Isma'il, and he added in the hadith of Jarir: "The Book of Allah contains guidance and light; whoever holds fast to it and takes hold of it is upon guidance, and whoever misses it goes astray."

And Muhammad ibn Bakkar ibn al-Rayyan narrated to us, Hassan—meaning Ibn Ibrahim—narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Masruq, from Yazid ibn Hayyan, from Zayd ibn Arqam, from the Prophet (pbuh)... and he related the hadith similarly, with the meaning of the hadith of Zuhayr.

Zuhayr ibn Harb and Shuja' ibn Makhlad both narrated to me from Ibn 'Ulayyah—Zuhayr said: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—Abu Hayyan narrated to me, Yazid ibn Hayyan narrated to me, who said: Husayn ibn Sabrah, 'Umar ibn Muslim, and I set out to Zayd ibn Arqam. When we sat with him, Husayn said to him: "You have encountered much good, O Zayd! You saw the Messenger of Allah (pbuh), heard his speech, fought alongside him in battle, and prayed behind him; you have indeed encountered much good, O Zayd. Narrate to us, O Zayd, what you heard from the Messenger of Allah (pbuh)." He said: "O son of my brother, by Allah, my age has advanced, my time has grown old, and I have forgotten some of what I used to retain from the Messenger of Allah (pbuh). So whatever I narrate to you, accept it; and whatever I do not, do not burden me with it." Then he said: One day the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) stood up to deliver a sermon among us by a water spring called Khumm, between Mecca and Medina. He praised Allah, extolled Him, exhorted and reminded, then said: "To proceed: Behold, O people! I am only a human being; soon the messenger of my Lord will come and I will respond. And I am leaving among you two weighty things: the first of them is the Book of Allah, in which is guidance and light, so take hold of the Book of Allah and adhere firmly to it." Thus he exhorted regarding the Book of Allah and encouraged devotion to it. Then he said: "And the people of my household: I remind you of Allah concerning the people of my household! I remind you of Allah concerning the people of my household! I remind you of Allah concerning the people of my household!" Husayn said to him: "And who are the people of his household, O Zayd? Are his wives not of the people of his household?" He said: "His wives are of the people of his household, but the people of his household are those who are forbidden from accepting charity after him." He asked: "And who are they?" He said: "They are the family of 'Ali, the family of 'Aqil, the family of Ja'far, and the family of 'Abbas." He asked: "All of those were forbidden from accepting charity?" He said: "Yes."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Hatim—meaning Ibn Isma'il—narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi 'Ubayd, from Salamah ibn al-Akwa', who said: 'Ali had remained behind from the Prophet (pbuh) at Khaybar, for he was suffering from an eye ailment. Then he said: "Shall I remain behind from the Messenger of Allah (pbuh)?" So 'Ali set out and caught up with the Prophet (pbuh). On the evening of the night following which morning Allah granted victory, the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: "I will certainly give the banner—or the banner will certainly be taken—tomorrow by a man whom Allah and His Messenger love—or he said: who loves Allah and His Messenger—through whom Allah will grant victory." Suddenly we saw 'Ali, while we were not expecting him. They said: "Here is 'Ali!" So the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) gave him the banner, and Allah granted victory through him.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz—meaning Ibn Abi Hazim—narrated to us, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl; (H) and Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us—and the wording is this—Ya'qub—meaning Ibn 'Abd al-Rahman—narrated to us, from Abu Hazim, Sahl ibn Sa'd informed me that the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said on the day of Khaybar: "I will certainly give this banner to a man at whose hands Allah will grant victory, who loves Allah and His Messenger, and whom Allah and His Messenger love." He said: The people spent that night discussing among themselves which of them would be given it. He said: When morning came, the people went to the Messenger of Allah (pbuh), each of them hoping to be given it. He said: "Where is 'Ali ibn Abi Talib?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, he is complaining of his eyes." He said: So they sent for him, and he was brought. The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) spat in his eyes and supplicated for him, and he was cured as though he had never had any pain. Then he gave him the banner. 'Ali said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall I fight them until they become like us?" He said: "Proceed steadily until you arrive in their midst, then call them to Islam and inform them of what is obligatory upon them of Allah's right therein. For by Allah, that Allah should guide a single man through you is better for you than possessing red camels."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Ya'qub—meaning Ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Qari—narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said on the day of Khaybar: "I will certainly give this banner to a man who loves Allah and His Messenger, and Allah will grant victory at his hands." 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "I never desired command except on that day." He said: "So I craned my neck toward it, hoping that I would be called for it." He said: Then the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) called 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, gave it to him, and said: "March forward and do not turn back until Allah grants you victory." He said: 'Ali walked a little, then stopped without turning around and called out: "O Messenger of Allah, upon what should I fight the people?" He said: "Fight them until they bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. If they do that, they have protected their blood and their wealth from you, except by its right, and their reckoning is with Allah."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Ghundar narrated to us, from Shu'bah; (H) and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar both narrated to us—they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, I heard Ibrahim ibn Sa'd from Sa'd, from the Prophet (pbuh), that he said to 'Ali: "Are you not pleased that you should be to me of the status that Harun was to Musa?"

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id and Muhammad ibn 'Abbad narrated to us—and their words were close—they said: Hatim—and he is Ibn Isma'il—narrated to us, from Bukayr ibn Mismar, from 'Amir ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, from his father, who said: Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan commanded Sa'd and said: "What prevented you from reviling Abu al-Turab?" He replied: "As for what I recall of three things that the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said to him, I will never revile him; for me to possess even one of them is more beloved to me than red camels. I heard the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) say to him when he left him behind in one of his military expeditions, and 'Ali said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah, have you left me behind with the women and children?' So the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said to him: 'Are you not pleased that you should be to me of the status that Harun was to Musa, except that there is no prophethood after me?' And I heard him saying on the day of Khaybar: 'I will certainly give the banner to a man who loves Allah and His Messenger, and whom Allah and His Messenger love.' He said: So we craned our necks for it, and he said: 'Call 'Ali for me.' He was brought while suffering from an eye ailment, so he spat in his eye and handed the banner to him, and Allah granted victory through him. And when this verse was revealed: 'Say: Come, let us call our sons and your sons,' the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) called 'Ali, Fatimah, Hasan, and Husayn, and said: 'O Allah, these are my family.'"
Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, in this chain of narration.

And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Ghundar narrated to us, from Shu'bah; (H) and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar both narrated to us—they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) left 'Ali ibn Abi Talib behind during the expedition of Tabuk. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, do you leave me behind among the women and children?" He said: "Are you not pleased that you should be to me of the status that Harun was to Musa, except that there is no prophet after me?"

Yahya ibn Yahya al-Tamimi, Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah, 'Ubaydullah al-Qawariri, and Surayj ibn Yunus all narrated to us from Yusuf al-Majishun—and the wording is Ibn al-Sabbah's—Yusuf Abu Salamah al-Majishun narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from 'Amir ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said to 'Ali: "You are to me of the status that Harun was to Musa, except that there is no prophet after me." Sa'id said: I wished to hear it directly from Sa'd's mouth, so I met Sa'd and related to him what 'Amir had narrated to me. He said: "I heard it." I said: "Did you hear it yourself?" He placed his two fingers upon his ears and said: "Yes, or may they both become deaf!"

Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Hulwani and Abu Bakr ibn Ishaq both narrated to us—they said: Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Kathir narrated to us, Sharik ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Namir informed me, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) went out one day to a garden in Medina for his need, and I went out following in his footsteps... and he related the hadith with the meaning of the hadith of Sulayman ibn Bilal, and he mentioned in the hadith: Ibn al-Musayyab said: "So I interpreted that as being their graves: they gathered together here, while 'Uthman was separated."

Abu Bakr ibn Ishaq narrated it to me, Sa'id ibn 'Ufayr narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Bilal narrated to me, Sharik ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Namir narrated to me: I heard Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab saying: Abu Musa al-Ash'ari narrated to me right here—and Sulayman pointed to the gathering place of Sa'id in the direction of the Maqsurah. Abu Musa said: I went out seeking the Messenger of Allah (pbuh), and found that he had gone into the enclosed gardens. I followed him and found that he had entered a garden, sat on the raised stone edge of the well, and bared his shins and dangled them into the well... and he related the hadith with the meaning of the hadith of Yahya ibn Hassan, and he did not mention the statement of Sa'id: "So I interpreted them as their graves."

Muhammad ibn Miskin al-Yamami narrated to us, Yahya ibn Hassan narrated to us, Sulayman—and he is Ibn Bilal—narrated to us, from Sharik ibn Abi Namir, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Abu Musa al-Ash'ari informed me that he performed ablution in his house, then went out and said: "I will certainly stay close to the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) and be with him throughout this day of mine." He said: So he came to the mosque and asked about the Prophet (pbuh), and they said: "He went out and headed in this direction." He said: So I set out following his tracks, asking about him until he entered the well of Aris. He said: I sat by the gate—and its gate was made of date-palm branches—until the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) had relieved himself and performed ablution. I stood up and went to him, and behold, he had sat upon the well of Aris, in the middle of its raised edge, bared his shins, and dangled them into the well. He said: I greeted him with salam, then turned away and sat by the gate, saying: "I will surely be the doorkeeper of the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) today." Abu Bakr came and pushed the gate, so I said: "Who is this?" He said: "Abu Bakr." I said: "Wait a moment." He said: Then I went and said: "O Messenger of Allah, here is Abu Bakr asking permission to enter." He said: "Admit him and give him the glad tidings of Paradise." He said: So I went back and said to Abu Bakr: "Enter, and the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) gives you the glad tidings of Paradise." He said: So Abu Bakr entered and sat on the right of the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) with him on the raised edge, and dangled his legs into the well as the Prophet (pbuh) had done, baring his shins. Then I returned and sat down, and I had left my brother performing ablution to catch up with me. I said: "If Allah intends good for so-and-so"—meaning his brother—"He will bring him." Then someone shook the gate, so I said: "Who is this?" He said: "'Umar ibn al-Khattab." I said: "Wait a moment." Then I came to the Messenger of Allah (pbuh), greeted him with salam, and said: "Here is 'Umar asking permission to enter." He said: "Admit him and give him the glad tidings of Paradise." So I came to 'Umar and said: "He has granted permission, and the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) gives you the glad tidings of Paradise." He said: So he entered and sat with the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) on the raised edge on his left, and dangled his legs into the well. Then I returned and sat down, and said: "If Allah intends good for so-and-so"—meaning his brother—"He will bring him." Then a person came and shook the gate, so I said: "Who is this?" He said: "'Uthman ibn 'Affan." I said: "Wait a moment." He said: And I came to the Prophet (pbuh) and informed him. He said: "Admit him and give him the glad tidings of Paradise along with an affliction that will befall him." He said: So I came and said: "Enter, and the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) gives you the glad tidings of Paradise along with an affliction that will befall you." He said: So he entered, and found that the raised edge was occupied, so he sat opposite them on the other side. Sharik said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: "So I interpreted that as being their graves."

Abu al-Rabi' al-'Ataki narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, that the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) entered a garden and ordered me to guard the gate... with the meaning of the hadith of 'Uthman ibn Ghiyath.
